Record by gradeDo higher grades win more often?

Every graded sharp pick is grouped by its 1 to 9 grade. The grade is built from patterns found in the Nov 7 to 9 games, so that backtest will look good by design and says little. Only games from Nov 10 on are a fair test: if the grade works, the higher groups should win more often there over time.

Team scatter recordDid the adjusted team ratings agree with the pick?

For every graded sharp pick on the spread or total, did the two teams' ratings (the team scatter check on each game) point to the same side as the pick? It counts games from Nov 10 on. Nov 10 and 11 used CBB Analytics' plain team stats (not adjusted for opponents) and Nov 13 on uses a matchup of the four factors (shooting, turnovers, offensive rebounds, free throws), each team's offense against the other's defense, adjusted for opponents with CBB Analytics' Team Scatter, so the two periods are not the same test, and it needs about 50 games before it means much. It is not part of the 1 to 9 grade.

Pinnacle and Circa recordDid the sharpest line and Circa back the sharp picks?

Every graded sharp DraftKings pick on the spread or total, grouped by what Pinnacle and Circa showed at the time. Pinnacle "confirms" when its own line moved 0.5 or more toward the sharp side since its first reading, "flat" when it stayed within 0.5, and "against" when it moved the other way. Circa agrees or disagrees when its own splits show the same or the other side sharp. Nov 7 to 11 used VSiN's DraftKings splits and Nov 12 on uses Owls' (the two disagree a lot), and Nov 7 to 9 is where the idea was found, so only Nov 10 on is a fair test. Picks are graded flat at -110 against the DraftKings line, win % ignores pushes, and the samples are small.

Rule watchTwo experiments we are tracking

We are testing two rules. Both were picked after looking at Nov 7 to 9, so those records (the backtest) say very little. Only games from Nov 10 on are a fair test, and we need about 50 of them before a record means much.

  • Total rule: original system, all three checks pass, and the handle is 10 to 49 points above the bets.
  • Spread rule: KenPom side, KenPom's team is the sharp side, and that team is favored by more than 3 and up to 8 points.

How to read thisPlain-English guide to the terms
What is this page?
Each day we compare a computer prediction (KenPom) with what Vegas is offering, then look at where the big money is going. The list on the left shows every game with its grade. Click a game to see everything we found about it. After the games finish we grade every pick so you can see how it did.
KenPom
A college basketball ratings site (kenpom.com) that predicts the winner, the margin and the total points of every game.
Vegas line (DraftKings)
The spread, total and money line the sportsbook offers. We also look at how the line moved since it opened.
Bets and handle
Bets is the share of tickets on a side (how many people). Handle is the share of dollars on a side. Example: 60% of the money but only 40% of the tickets means a few big wagers.
Grade (1 to 9)
A sharp pick's score, 1 plus up to 8 points, built from the two patterns we are tracking. Spread: the side is favored by more than 3 and up to 8 points (4 points), the sharp gap is 15 to 30 (3 points), and the handle is 65 to 80% (1 point). Total: the line moved toward the side (3 points), the sharp gap is 10 to 49 (3 points), and KenPom's total is 2 to 6 points off the line (2 points). The money line has no pattern yet, so it keeps the older strength score. In the list, 7 to 9 is green, 4 to 6 is amber and 1 to 3 is gray, and a game shows its best pick. These patterns were found by looking back at Nov 7 to 9, so the grades fit those games and the real test is games from Nov 10 on. Only sharp picks get a grade.
Team scatter
A second look, on every game's page, at CBB Analytics' Team Scatter ratings: each team's offense, defense and pace, adjusted for the strength of the opponents it has played. We add the two teams' ratings into a rough "scatter total" and "scatter margin" and see whether it points the same way as each sharp pick on the spread or total. It replaced the earlier style check, which used plain team stats. It is an experiment and is not part of the grade. Teams have played only 1 to 4 games, so the ratings swing a lot, and "Too early" means a team has played just one game.
Pinnacle
The sharpest sportsbook, whose line moves first when professional money comes in. On each game's page we show its line from its first reading to the time of the splits. For a sharp pick it is confirms when its line moved 0.5 or more toward that side, flat within 0.5, and against the other way.
Circa
A Las Vegas sportsbook that publishes its own bets and handle. We read its splits the same way (money at least 10 points ahead of tickets means sharp) and show whether it picks the same side as DraftKings (agrees) or the other side (disagrees). It is a small book, so readings of 0% and 100% are called thin data.
Do the checks agree?
The card at the top of each game's page. It lines up KenPom, DraftKings money, Pinnacle's line, Circa's money and the team scatter check on the spread and the total, and shades each one green if it points to the same side as DraftKings' sharp side and red if it points to the other side.
Sharp
A side where the handle is at least 10 points above the bets. Big money tends to come from experienced bettors.
Public
Everything else: the bets are higher than the handle, or the two are within 10 points.
All three
Three checks pass: KenPom and Vegas point at different sides (or KenPom picked the side), the money is sharp on it, and the line has moved toward that side since it opened.
Original system
KenPom and Vegas disagree, and we look at Vegas's side. For totals it is the side KenPom does not lean toward.
KenPom side
We look at the side KenPom picked (or the Over or Under it leans toward), whether or not Vegas agrees.
Spread, total, money line
Spread: who wins by how many points. Total: Over or Under the combined score. Money line: who wins outright. The money line is only screened when the spread is under 6 points.
Units and results
One unit is risked on every game. Spread and total are graded at -110 (win about 0.91 units, lose 1). Money lines use their own odds.
Small samples
We only have a few days of games, so every record here can change a lot. This page compares data sources and is not betting advice.
Where the numbers come fromSources, timing and limits
Snapshot
KenPom from —, bets and handle from —, lines from —. Lines and splits keep moving, so a game can change by tip-off.
KenPom
Winner, margin, win probability and total come from the KenPom FanMatch page. Early in the season the ratings still lean on preseason priors.
Bets and handle
DraftKings splits come from the Owls Insight feed from Nov 12 on (Nov 7 to 11 came from VSiN, whose numbers often differ a lot). Pinnacle lines and Circa splits also come from Owls, read at the same time as the DraftKings splits.
Team ratings
Opponent-adjusted offensive rating, defensive rating and pace from CBB Analytics' Team Scatter tool (Division I, full season), read at the same time as the lines. Before Nov 13 the page used CBB Analytics' plain team stats instead.
Lines and movement
Opening and current lines come from DraftKings through ESPN's odds feed. "Moved toward" means the side got stronger since the open: a smaller spread number, shorter odds, or a total that moved toward it. It is shown on every sharp pick but not required.
Money line math
The market probability is the implied probability of the odds as quoted, with the bookmaker's margin left in.
Left out
Games that had already started when the lines were pulled, games without a DraftKings line or a KenPom prediction, and, for the money line only, games with a spread of 6 or more.
Limits
Very small markets can show a huge handle from one or two tickets. Some opening totals look like early placeholders.
